18.description: Saskatoon's Bus Rapid Transit (Link) project is on track for partial 2028 implementation, with ongoing construction, fleet renewal, and network redesign.

chips.text: Received as information
6 for, 0 against
Council discussed moving to bi-annual project updates for the BRT Link.
Administration advises against contraflow on First Avenue for safety and operational reasons.

19.description: Saskatoon reviews 2025 summer road maintenance, including street sweeping and sidewalk repairs. Plans for 2026 include improving work zone safety and exploring AI for pothole inspections.

chips.text: Received as information
6 for, 0 against
Staff noted AI for pothole inspections is expensive, in its infancy, and lacks budget.

20.description: Council approved the Saskatoon Accessibility Advisory Committee's 2026 work plan, detailing its planned activities for the year.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Chair noted the committee did a great job, as no questions were asked.

21.description: The committee recommends approving new criteria for prioritizing where to build sidewalks and cycling facilities, including an equity component for underserved areas. This aims to guide future active transportation investments.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Prioritization criteria consider youth, seniors, low-income, immigrants, Indigenous
Establishes the first formal prioritization process for new cycling facility projects.
Equity criteria prioritize areas where residents have lower car ownership and need active transport.

24.description: The committee recommends amending a policy to create more on-street accessible parking, especially in pay parking zones. Businesses can request new spaces, funded by the city.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
The number of regular parking spaces that will be impacted is currently unknown.
Saskatoon Accessibility Advisory Committee supported the changes and emphasized the need.
A $75,000 capital project will fund new accessible parking spaces in 2027.

26.description: The committee recommends amending the Vehicles for Hire Bylaw to standardize taxi equipment, increase cleaning fees, and change the van rate to a flat large vehicle fare of $9.50.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Delegate noted report's vehicle and fuel costs are outdated compared to current reality.
Taxi drivers' income on long trips may decrease with new van rate.
Administration does not regulate operational relationships between brokers and drivers.
No timeframe given for a proposed city-wide taxi deposit system.
Taxi drivers and union leadership largely oppose the proposed van rate change.
Low-income passengers sharing rides may be affected by van rate changes.
Staff is developing a proposal for city-wide taxi deposit systems.

9.description: Saskatoon updated its criteria for prioritizing new sidewalks and cycling infrastructure, adding an equity component to focus investments in areas with high social needs.

chips.text: Received as information
5 for, 0 against
Seniors' priority for new sidewalks was reduced from 15 to 5 points.
The prioritization process does not address how projects are distributed across city wards.
New criteria prioritize sidewalk and cycling projects in areas with youth, seniors, low-income
Administration will present a 10-year summary of the Active Transportation Plan progress in June.

22.description: Saskatoon is planning future major road projects, including Circle Drive and Preston Avenue, to prepare for growth and secure funding.

chips.text: Councilor Donauer questioned plans for 60th, Marquis, and 71st Street intersections.
Residents near future freeway connections and north end intersections.
Administration will report on accelerating planning before next budget.

23.description: Saskatoon will allow Neuron to operate 500 shared electric kick scooters from 2026 to 2029, following Bird's exit from the program.

25.description: Saskatoon will pilot removing 13 of 14 pay stations on Central Avenue for one year, testing digital payment options to assess cost savings and feasibility for future parking management.

chips.text: Councillor Peers questioned equity for those without smartphones or unwilling to use apps.
The pilot tests managing pay parking without physical stations for future city expansions.
Councillor Peers reported hearing from many residents concerned about not having smartphones.
Pilot reduces service for those without smartphones, older residents, or limited data access.
Administration will report pilot results to Council in Q4 2027.
